name: swarmdeck
description: Torrents from a web page, on a phone or a computer. WebTorrent in the browser, pieces in OPFS; on a computer, a list with table view, search, multi-select, drop anywhere, shortcuts, save into a folder. .torrent editor built in. Your own server or TorBox, put.io, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid for unreachable swarms. Installable offline PWA.

paragraphs: Torrents from a web page, on a phone or a computer. Add a .torrent or a magnet, watch it arrive, save the files to the device; share files of your own, edit, make and check .torrent files — and when the swarm is one a browser cannot reach, hand the same torrent to a real client: one you run in a container, or an account you already pay for.

On a phone it is one column you can install like an app. On a computer it is a list of torrents beside the one open, with a table view, a search, several selected at once, files and folders dropped anywhere on the window, the keyboard, and files saved straight into a folder.
The page itself is static — HTML, CSS and two vendored libraries, hosted on GitHub Pages. Everything else is optional and yours: nothing is enabled until you give it a key or an address.

requirements.text: The event log in the details panel says what was tried: the trackers, then the metadata caches, then the retry. "Blocked by CORS" there means the proxy in proxy/ would fix it.

It covers the file list, pause/resume, coming back from a frozen tab (the page is hidden, then shown, and the torrent must go looking for peers by itself), the share panel (the real link, selected, and the copy button answering on itself), Simple hiding every expert setting while Expert shows them and the choice surviving a reload, the details panel, saving the .torrent,…
